task.title: The sidebar divider should stop at the board header's bottom edge
task.description:
With the title strip (PR #162), the sidebar's 1px right border runs from the bottom of the window all the way to the top, cutting through the title row and the board's header band. Dylan: the vertical line should stop where it meets the horizontal border under the board header, so the title strip, the sidebar head and the board header read as one connected layer, and the divider only separates the sidebar from the board body below that line.

The two lines come from different documents: the vertical one is #sidebar's border-right in the shell (desktop/src/renderer/styles.css), the horizontal one is .app-header's border-bottom in the Go-served board page (internal/webui/assets/index.html), drawn inside the board WebContentsView whose left edge sits exactly on the sidebar's right edge. The shell cannot know the header's height (it depends on the board's content), so the board page should draw the vertical divider below its own header when it is embedded in Workbench, and the shell should draw none while a board is showing. The board view already has a preload (desktop/src/preload/board.js) that can mark the document as embedded; a plain browser must never see the divider. On the shell's own views (import, Next) the divider starts below the title strip so the strip stays one bar; on Linux, where there is no strip, it runs full height as before. Verify in a dev launch with screenshots in both themes: no vertical line anywhere in the top band, a clean corner where the two lines meet under the board header.
